items.title: Blocked Kentucky Visa Rule Threatens 10,000 International Students
items.subtitle: A new restriction could halt enrollment for thousands of overseas scholars.
items.imageQuery: Kentucky university campus, student passport, protest
items.detail: A Kentucky state court blocked a new rule that would have stopped many international students from enrolling because their visas wouldn’t meet a narrow definition. If the rule had taken effect, roughly 10,000 scholars could have been forced out, hurting both the students and the state’s universities that rely on their tuition and research contributions. The decision keeps current enrollment intact, but the fight may continue. Watch for any revised legislation and stay in touch with your school’s international office for updates on compliance.

items.title: Federal Judge Halts F‑1 Visa Limit to Four Years
items.subtitle: Court decision restores longer stay options for U.S. graduate students.
items.imageQuery: courtroom gavel, international student, university building
items.detail: A federal judge struck down a recent policy that capped F‑1 student visas at four years, restoring the ability for graduate students to stay longer while they finish degrees or conduct research. This ruling means students can now plan multi‑year programs without fearing an abrupt visa expiration. It also reassures universities that rely on international talent. Keep an eye on any appeals and check with your university’s visa advisors to ensure your paperwork reflects the longer stay option.

items.title: UK Student Visa 2026: Key Changes for Indian Applicants
items.subtitle: Essential updates on fees, work rights and application timelines.
items.imageQuery: London skyline, Indian student, visa documents
items.detail: The UK government announced several changes to its 2026 student visa scheme that affect Indian applicants. Fees will rise modestly, but work‑hour allowances increase, letting students work up to 30 hours weekly during term. Application windows open earlier, and a new points‑based assessment adds weight to English proficiency and funding proof. These tweaks aim to attract more Indian scholars while ensuring they can support themselves. Prospective applicants should start gathering documents now and monitor the UK Home Office website for the exact rollout dates.

items.title: Study‑Abroad Trends: Visa Tightening and Rising Costs Shift Choices
items.subtitle: How tighter rules and price hikes are reshaping where students go abroad.
items.imageQuery: airplane boarding, world map, student backpack
items.source: Polsky Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation
items.detail: New data shows tighter visa rules and soaring tuition are pushing students to rethink where they study abroad. Countries with more flexible entry policies and lower living costs, like Canada and some European nations, are seeing enrollment bumps, while traditional destinations such as the U.S. face declines. This shift could reshape campus demographics and scholarship funding. Students should compare total costs—including visa fees and work rights—across options and stay alert for scholarship programs that offset rising expenses.

items.title: Top 8 Best‑Value Public Universities in New York
items.subtitle: Affordable schools that still rank among the nation’s best.
items.imageQuery: college campus, tuition sign, New York state map
items.detail: New York’s public universities are proving you don’t need a private‑school price tag to get a top education. Schools like SUNY Binghamton, Stony Brook, and Buffalo consistently rank high nationally while keeping tuition well below the private‑college average. Strong research programs, vibrant campus life, and robust alumni networks add value. If cost is a concern, explore these institutions, apply early for state aid, and consider living off‑campus to stretch your budget further.

items.title: Forbes: 1% Student‑Loan Interest Cut – Deadline Approaches
items.subtitle: Act now to lower your loan cost before the September cutoff.
items.detail: Forbes reported a temporary 1 % cut in student‑loan interest rates that expires at the end of September. Borrowers who refinance or enroll in an income‑driven repayment plan before the deadline will lock in lower monthly payments, saving thousands over the life of the loan. Act quickly: check your loan servicer’s portal, compare offers, and submit the required paperwork now to avoid missing the cut‑off.

items.title: Brookfield‑Scion $1.4B Refinance of 25,000 Student‑Housing Beds
items.subtitle: Major financing boost for affordable campus housing supply.
items.imageQuery: student dormitory, construction crane, financial chart
items.detail: Brookfield‑Scion secured a $1.4 billion refinance for 25,000 student‑housing beds, injecting fresh capital into affordable dormitories across the country. The funding will upgrade aging facilities, add modern amenities, and expand capacity where demand outpaces supply. For students, this means more options for reasonably priced on‑campus living, especially in high‑cost markets. Keep an eye on your university’s housing announcements, as renovations or new constructions may roll out over the next few years.

items.title: Rice University Scholarship Recipients Celebrate Donor Support
items.subtitle: Students honored for academic excellence and community impact.
items.imageQuery: students on stage, scholarship plaque, rice campus
items.detail: Rice University honored a group of scholars with a new donor‑funded scholarship that recognizes academic excellence and community service. Recipients receive tuition assistance and mentorship opportunities, easing financial pressure and fostering leadership. The program highlights the impact of private philanthropy on student success. If you’re at Rice, look for upcoming application cycles and consider how community involvement can strengthen your candidacy for similar awards.

items.title: Hendrix College Announces New Endowed Scholarship
items.subtitle: Funding opens for undergraduates pursuing liberal arts majors.
items.imageQuery: college quad, scholarship award, student reading
items.detail: Hendrix College launched an endowed scholarship aimed at undergraduates pursuing liberal‑arts majors. The fund provides renewable awards that cover tuition and, in some cases, living expenses, making a Hendrix education more accessible. The college hopes the scholarship will attract diverse talent and encourage interdisciplinary study. Current and prospective students should check the college’s financial‑aid portal for eligibility criteria and application deadlines.

items.title: Undergraduate Engineers Win Summer Research Scholarships from General Atomics
items.subtitle: Hands‑on projects in aerospace and energy for rising engineers.
items.imageQuery: engineering lab, solar panel, student team
items.detail: A team of undergraduate engineers earned summer research scholarships from General Atomics, granting them hands‑on experience in aerospace and energy projects. The program pairs students with industry mentors, offering stipends, lab access, and the chance to contribute to real‑world innovations. Winners will present their findings at a campus symposium, boosting their resumes. If you’re an engineering major, watch for future calls and consider building relationships with faculty who can recommend you for similar opportunities.
